The Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) with 100,000 members nationally and
important experience in organizing campaigns, should put itself forward as a
leader of the movement against the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. In fact, for the
good of the American anti-war movement, for the good of the Iranian people and
the people of the region, it is important that DSA take the lead.

The war, now a regional war affecting the entire world, has already claimed
thousands of lives and it will kill many more. Many of the victims are
civilians, like the 150 children killed by an American missile at a girls
school in Iran. U.S. soldiers have also been killed. The war will lead to
rising prices for gasoline and everything else, affecting the entire American
and the economy worldwide. Working people here in America and around the world
will pay the price, in fact they are already paying with their lives and their
well-being.

The groups now attempting to lead the anti-war movement—the Workers World
Party, the Party of Socialism and Liberation (PSL), and ANSWER—will make it
impossible to build a strong, healthy movement that can attract the American
people. All of those groups have for years supported the Islamic Republic of
Iran, a theocratic totalitarian state that has killed tens of thousands of its
citizens for participating in pro-democracy protests. The American people will
not want to march against the Iran war under the flags of the Islamic
Republic.

Those groups argue that because Iran has been an enemy of the United States
and Israel, and because it is now fighting them, that the Iranian government
is an anti-imperialist nation that deserves our political support. Their
position of support for the Iranian state made it impossible for them to rally
or even to offer full-throated support to the “Woman, Life, Freedom” movement
in Iran in 2022 or the reform movement protests of 2025-26.

Some in DSA want to join with Workers World, PSL, and ANSWER to build the
antiwar movement. That would be a grave political mistake. DSA members should
consider how their association with pro-Iranian government groups will affect
their electoral campaigns and their elected officials. Zohran Mamdani’s
mayoralty and the campaigns of other DSA members will be jeopardized by such
an alliance. _The New York Times_ and other news media will conduct
investigations that reveal such connections. _The New York Post, Fox News_ and
other rightwing media will publicize the association in an attempt to
discredit DSA.

Rather than joining the small, existing anti-war movement with its current
leaders, DSA, with its large numbers, talented members, and organizing
experience, should put itself forth as a leader of the movement. It should
enter into a coalition with the groups that have organized the No Kings
protests, most of whom are liberal democrats and independents, and many of
whom are progressive activists, while some are democratic socialist. DSA
should organize with them. As all good organizers have always done, DSA should
organize those to its _right_ , not those like PSL who falsely claim to stand
on the left. There is nothing leftist about supporting the authoritarian
governments of Iran, Russia, and China as those groups have.

DSA, unlike Workers World, PSL, and ANSWER, should at the same time
demonstrate a consistent anti-imperialism, opposing the imperialist wars of
Israel and the United States, but also opposing Russian imperialism and
supporting Ukraine. Support for Ukraine means defending its right to
sovereignty and self-determination, including its right to get arms wherever
it can.

When an organization campaigns, whether for a candidate or for a cause, it
changes itself and it changes its relationship with other groups and with the
public. A serious DSA anti-war campaign, based on democratic socialist
principles, calling for ending the war on Iran and self-determination for the
Iranian people, will bring out the best in DSA, clarifying its politics and
unifying its membership.

DSA has the numbers and the wherewithal to play a leading role in the anti-war
movement with allies like those in No Kings, and it should step up now.
